subject: Computer Networking
title: Industrial IoT and Private 5G
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Industrial IoT and Private 5G.

hook.text: Factories deploy private 5G on their floors. They own the network end-to-end, no carrier needed.

buildup.text: Private 5G guarantees low latency. Robots and sensors need reliability that Wi-Fi can't match.

discovery.text: IIoT connects machines, conveyors, and sensors. Real-time data enables predictive maintenance.

twist.text: Predicting failures before they happen avoids millions in downtime. The network pays for itself.

climax.text: Industry 4.0, smart factories, and reshoring all rely on private industrial networks.

punchline.text: Private 5G turns the factory floor into one connected nervous system.

quiz.question: Why do factories deploy private 5G instead of using Wi-Fi?
options: Private 5G offers guaranteed low latency and reliability that Wi-Fi can't match
Wi-Fi is too expensive for industrial use
Private 5G doesn't require any radio spectrum

details.summary: Private 5G networks give factories and industrial sites dedicated cellular coverage with guaranteed latency, bandwidth, and security.
details.whyItMatters: Industrial automation demands network reliability that shared public networks cannot provide. Private 5G enables factories to wirelessly connect equipment with celluar-grade reliability and sub-10-millisecond latency.
takeaways: Private 5G provides dedicated cellular coverage for industrial sites
Sub-10-millisecond latency enables real-time robotic control
Dedicated spectrum eliminates interference from public users

faq.question: Why use private 5G instead of Wi-Fi for industrial IoT?
faq.answer: Wi-Fi uses unlicensed spectrum subject to interference and has inconsistent latency. Private 5G uses licensed or shared spectrum with guaranteed quality of service. It supports seamless mobility for AGVs and robots.

faq.question: Who can deploy a private 5G network?
faq.answer: Regulators in many countries allocate spectrum for private use. Germany, UK, Japan, and others offer dedicated industrial spectrum. Companies deploy small cells across their facility with a local core network.
